Class Trainer

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.client.Trainer
All Implemented Interfaces:
AgentSession
Direct Known Subclasses:
FightLearnSession, ReplicaTrainer, TrainingSession
abstract class Trainer extends Object implements AgentSession
Training as such: which fight comes next, what a step was worth, when the network learns from what it has gathered, and when a stage is passed. Everything here is the same whatever body the agent has. The body is the subclass's business: TrainingSession plays the user's own character and sees the screen; HeadlessSession plays a fake player and sees a drawn picture.

One thread drives a trainer from start to stop: the client thread for the first, the server thread for the second. The PPO update is the only part that runs elsewhere.

    • DRILL_CRIT_ZONE

      private static final float DRILL_CRIT_ZONE
      The first crit drill: the distance, eye to hitbox, within which it wants the jump made. Only with the opponent right in its face. Farther off, and that includes the whole range sprint hits are made at, a jump made in the drill gets no swing and is charged.

      It is drawn this tight on purpose. What the drill teaches becomes a habit, and a habit can be added to later but not taken back: in real fights it can find that a jump from a little farther pays as well, and take that up; it could never have unlearned jumping at sprint-hit range.

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • PUNISH_DRILL_KNOCKBACK

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • episodeLockedDrill

      boolean episodeLockedDrill
      And one in which it is held, as in all of those that come first, before the stage's own fights, and in two in three of those that go on after them: the fighter cannot walk, strafe, sprint or turn. Its camera is kept on the opponent for it, and all it has is the jump key and the swing. With no W there is no sprint, so a swing made on the way down with the sword charged is a critical hit and nothing else can get in the way of finding that out. In the drill for the punish crit it has not even the jump: the opponent's hit is what puts it in the air.

      Held for the first crit drill: how near the opponent has to be for a jump to be wanted. While it is the lesson, right in its face (DRILL_CRIT_ZONE). Once the lessons are passed and the drill only goes on, the opponent is either there or out of reach altogether, and the line is drawn at a sword's reach: whether a jump from in between pays is then for the fights to settle, where it costs unless it lands, and the drill has nothing to say about it.

      A stage that has just begun may want a control put back to how a control starts (the jump key in the crit stage). Done once, before the stage is played; never while an update is running.

    • episodeKeys

      int episodeKeys()
      The keys the running fight is played with: the stage's, or in a locked crit drill only the jump and the swing. And in such a drill the swing only in the air: on the ground there is just the jump key, so every swing it makes is one a critical hit can come of, and a swing on the ground cannot use the sword up first.

    • onEqualTerms

      boolean onEqualTerms()
      Whether the running fight is one on equal terms: one set up that way (see StageSpec.fairShare), or one that came out that way. Only such a fight counts as won or lost against a copy of itself. One whose knockback comes late stays in reach after it is hit and swings back, while the fighter is thrown clear by every hit it takes: measured against the copy it was a minute before, it landed 38 hits a minute and took 57 where the knockback came a quarter to half a second late. One that is knocked back less is back in reach sooner, which is the same advantage in small, and a picture of the opponent that comes in fits and starts is the fighter's handicap alone. Those fights are there to be learned from.

    • actorNeedsExplained

      float actorNeedsExplained()
      The least share of a batch's returns the critic has to explain for the actor to learn from that batch. Nothing is asked in the arena. Against people it is: those fights are few, short and unlike anything the critic was trained on, and when it has no idea what a fight was worth, what the actor would learn from it is noise (0.13.2, fights on a server: the critic explained less than nothing of four batches in a row, and the actor was moved by each of them several times as far as a training update moves it).
